title: Reconsidering Screen Time as a Family
paragraphs: After noticing that family dinners had gradually devolved into each member silently scrolling personal devices rather than engaging in the meaningful conversation that had once characterized their shared evening meals, Farid proposed establishing device-free periods that initially met considerable resistance from his teenage children.

His children argued that the proposed restriction felt arbitrary and unfairly singled out their generation's communication habits, while Farid countered that the pattern affected every family member equally rather than representing generational criticism specifically.

Rather than simply imposing the rule unilaterally, Farid proposed a trial period with explicit family discussion afterward regarding whether the change had produced meaningful improvement worth the initial discomfort of adjustment.

After several weeks, even initially resistant family members acknowledged that dinner conversations had genuinely improved, though maintaining the practice required ongoing collective commitment rather than a single decisive agreement, as old habits repeatedly threatened to resurface without continued deliberate attention.
